_comment: SAMPLE FILE — every value below is fictional/illustrative. Do not publish a review generated from this file as-is. Copy it, replace every field with real data from an actual testing engagement, and delete this _comment key (it is not part of the schema and is ignored).

tester.name: Independent contractor
tester.relevantExperience: Six years building and maintaining automation workflows for agency clients, primarily in Zapier and n8n.

workflowsTested: Webhook intake from a form provider, enrichment via HTTP request, write to a CRM contact record
Scheduled daily CSV export from a spreadsheet to a Slack channel summary
Error-branch test: deliberately pointed the CRM write step at an invalid API key to observe failure handling
testing.methodology: Built three workflows covering webhook intake, scheduled batch sync and a deliberate-failure scenario. Ran the webhook and scheduled workflows daily for three weeks, logging every execution's duration and outcome in a spreadsheet. Submitted one support ticket and one community forum question during the window.

quantitativeFindings: Webhook-to-CRM workflow averaged 1.3 seconds end to end across roughly 140 logged executions
Scheduled CSV sync failed 2 of 21 scheduled runs, both due to a timeout on the spreadsheet provider's API, not n8n itself
Deliberate invalid-API-key test produced a clear error in the execution log within 2 seconds and did not silently continue
advantages: The execution log made it straightforward to see exactly which step failed and why, including the raw HTTP response body
Self-hosting the Starter-equivalent workflow on a small VPS cost about $6/mo, well under the $20/mo Cloud Starter price
The code node let us handle a date-format transform that had no equivalent built-in step
limitations: The visual canvas becomes hard to follow once a workflow passes about 15 nodes without sub-workflow grouping
Community nodes for the CRM we used were unmaintained and required a manual JSON-based workaround
Error notifications are not configured by default; you must explicitly wire a failure-branch step to get alerted
reliabilityIssues: One workflow silently stopped executing after a self-hosted instance restart on 2026-08-11; it required manually re-activating the workflow, which is not mentioned prominently in the getting-started docs
Two scheduled-sync failures during the test window traced to the third-party spreadsheet API rate-limiting us, not to n8n itself
supportInteractions: Community forum question about the webhook signature header received a reply in 18 hours with a working code sample
No formal support ticket submitted — Starter plan support is forum-only per the vendor's published plan comparison

pricingSources.claim: Starter plan is $20/mo billed annually, 2,500 executions/mo

conflictsOfInterest: None. Tester has no financial or employment relationship with n8n GmbH.

affiliateRelationship.detail: StackPipeline's n8n tool entry carries an affiliate link (n8n.partnerlinks.io/stackpipeline); this is disclosed via the site-wide affiliate disclosure and the in-article disclosure banner.

scorecard.evidenceNote: First working webhook workflow was live about 35 minutes after account creation, per timestamped notes
The code node covered the one transform the built-in nodes could not handle; branching and error paths worked as documented
Community node for our CRM was unmaintained; had to fall back to raw HTTP requests for two of six required calls
One silent stop after a self-hosted restart during the 3-week window; two other failures traced to a third-party API, not n8n
Self-hosted equivalent workload ran for about $6/mo in VPS costs against the $20/mo Cloud Starter price
Forum reply took 18 hours; official docs did not mention the restart/re-activation behavior we hit
